subject.title: refactor(daemon): split Windows task scheduler integration

question: After real Windows behavior proof is added, should the protected daemon refactor be accepted as a behavior-neutral cleanup?
rationale: The remaining gate is not a mechanical code repair: a maintainer must decide whether the submitted Windows runtime evidence is sufficient for a protected, availability-sensitive daemon refactor.

options.title: Request Windows runtime proof
options.body: Require a redacted after-fix run that demonstrates scheduled-task lifecycle behavior and the Startup-folder fallback before making the merge decision.

options.title: Accept test-only evidence
options.body: Merge based on the existing focused tests and CI while explicitly accepting the unobserved Windows runtime risk.

recommendation.title: Request Windows runtime proof
recommendation.body: Require a redacted after-fix run that demonstrates scheduled-task lifecycle behavior and the Startup-folder fallback before making the merge decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history identifies this contributor as the author of the affected scheduler split; confidence is low because independent current-main ownership history was not available in the review material.
